evidence: Ruff 0.16.9 reports ASYNC221 on `os.spawnl(m, "x")` where `m` is bound by `with os.P_WAIT as m:`: is_p_wait (crates/ruff_linter/src/rules/flake8_async/rules/blocking_process_invocation.rs:176) reads a name's value through find_assigned_value, and find_binding_value (crates/ruff_python_semantic/src/analyze/typing.rs:1273) takes a with-item binding's value. The ports' shared `p-wait-arg` utility has no with-item case, so ASYNC221 misses the call and the ASYNC220 candidate reports it instead. Fix both together, then drop this entry.

`from xml.sax.saxutils import XMLGenerator` imports an XML writer, not a parser. Bandit 1.9.4's import blacklist reports any imported name whose dotted path starts with `xml.sax` (bandit/core/blacklisting.py), so it steers toward defusedxml, which has no saxutils. xml.sax.saxutils defines no parse, parseString or make_parser (CPython 3.14.7: `python3 -I -c "import xml.sax.saxutils as s; print(dir(s))"` lists only XMLFilterBase, XMLGenerator, escape, quoteattr, unescape, prepare_input_source and its own imports), and XMLFilterBase parses only through a parent reader its caller supplies. The port does not report `from xml.sax.saxutils import ...` or `from xml.sax import saxutils`; B317 still reports xml.sax parse calls.

The annotation `'''\\` + newline + `list[int]'''` has the decoded value backslash, newline, `list[int]`. Ruff 0.16.9 reads such a string with parse_complex_type_annotation (crates/ruff_python_parser/src/typing.rs:85), which runs parse_expression on the value, accepts the leading line continuation and reports PYI020 at 32:4. Rerail's annotation grammar (native/src/code_rule_dsl/literal/annotation.rs, `expression`) refuses a value that begins with a backslash continuation, so the string gets an ERROR root and the port's `parse: annotation` never matches. Probes run with port-check.mts showed this: `"\\\nlist[int]"` is missed (ruff 1, rule 0), while `'''list\\` + newline + `[int]'''`, `"\N{...}ist[int]"` and `"\x6cist[int]"` all agree.

`__all__: list = ['b', "c", ((('a')))]`: Ruff's AST has no parentheses, so add_to_names (crates/ruff_python_semantic/src/model/all.rs:79) sees `'a'` as an ExprStringLiteral entry and F822 reports it at 11:31. The engine's Exports::add (native/src/code_rule_dsl/scope/usage.rs:587) reads the element through value::python::string_literal, which returns None for a parenthesized_expression. So no entry is recorded and `resolves.unresolved` cannot match; a probe `__all__ = ["a", ("b"), "c"]` misses `b` the same way.

`__all__ += "foo3", "foo2", "foo1"` is an implicit tuple: Ruff reads it as an Expr::Tuple (crates/ruff_python_semantic/src/model/all.rs:155) and reports all three entries. tree-sitter-python gives it as an expression_list, and the engine's extract (native/src/code_rule_dsl/scope/usage.rs, match on node kind) handles only list/tuple/parenthesized/call, so it records no entries. A probe `__all__ += "d", "e"` confirms the miss (Ruff 2, rule 0).

`__all__ = ("parenthesized_item"), "in", ("an_unparenthesized_tuple")` is a bare tuple, which Ruff reads as Expr::Tuple with three string entries (crates/ruff_python_semantic/src/model/all.rs:155). The engine's extract in native/src/code_rule_dsl/scope/usage.rs has no expression_list arm (and Exports::add does not unwrap the parenthesized elements), so none of the three entries is recorded and the rule misses all three.

The tuple element `("a_veeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeery_long_parenthesized_item")` (lines 206-208) is a parenthesized string. Ruff's parenthesis-free AST passes it to add_to_names as a string literal and reports it at 207:9. The engine's Exports::add (native/src/code_rule_dsl/scope/usage.rs:587) gets a parenthesized_expression, for which string_literal returns None, so the entry is never recorded.

The tuple element `(("c"))` (lines 213-215) is a doubly parenthesized string that Ruff reads as a plain string literal entry (crates/ruff_python_semantic/src/model/all.rs:79) and reports at 214:9. The engine's Exports::add does not unwrap parenthesized_expression elements (native/src/code_rule_dsl/scope/usage.rs:587), so no entry exists for `resolves.unresolved` to test.

`__all__ = "foo", "an" "implicitly_concatenated_second_item", not_a_string_literal` is a bare tuple. Ruff records the two string entries and only flags the third as INVALID_OBJECT (crates/ruff_python_semantic/src/model/all.rs:84-96), reporting 359:11 and 359:18. The engine's extract (native/src/code_rule_dsl/scope/usage.rs) has no expression_list arm and records no entries for it.

pydocstyle/bom.py starts with a UTF-8 BOM (bytes EF BB BF before `'''`). Ruff 0.16.9 reports D300 at 1:1 because its column ignores the BOM. The harness's pointOf (conformance/languages/runner.ts:223-224) counts the decoded U+FEFF as one code point, so the same docstring finding lands at 1:2. Both tools flag the same docstring, so the FP at 1:2 and the FN at 1:1 are one finding measured two ways. port-check.mts agrees with live Ruff on the file, compared by range.

Line 2 is `"a" "b` with the second string unterminated. Ruff's lexer emits an unterminated string as a string token (the fixture's own comment says so), and ISC001 pairs it. Rerail's grammar finds error regions covering 64% of this file and reads none of it (port-check: `source-incomplete: file did not parse: error regions cover 64% of it, first at line 2, column 5`), so the two tools' error recovery cannot be compared here.

`"a" "b" "c` ends in an unterminated string. Ruff reports two pairs here (3:1 and 3:5) from its lexer's recovery tokens. Rerail does not read the file: error regions cover 64% of it (port-check failure source-incomplete). The input is invalid Python, so there is nothing to compare.

Lines 4-5 are `"a" """b` / `c""" "d` with a trailing unterminated string. Ruff's finding at 4:1 comes from the token stream it recovers from that broken file. Rerail skips the file as unread because error regions cover 64% of it (port-check source-incomplete).

`f"a" f"b" f"c` ends in an unterminated f-string. Ruff reports the pair at 10:1 from its recovered tokens. Rerail does not read the file: port-check reports `file did not parse: error regions cover 64% of it`.

Lines 11-12, `f"a" f"""b` / `c""" f"d {e`, end in an unterminated f-string with an open replacement field. Ruff's 11:1 finding depends on its lexer recovery. Rerail reads none of this file because error regions cover 64% of it.

Line 2 is `'' '` with an unterminated string (the regression test for ruff issue 21023). Ruff pairs `''` with the recovered `'` token. Rerail parses this file only partly, and port-check reports `AST clauses ran outside 3 error region(s), first at line 2, column 4`. This finding lies in an error region, where the AST rule does not run.

`'' '' '` ends in an unterminated string. Ruff's 4:1 finding (`'' ''`) comes from the token stream it recovers. Rerail's grammar folds this line into one of the file's 3 syntax-error regions, and AST clauses do not run inside those (port-check source-partial). Rerail's grammar still reports the valid line 3 (`"" ""`), so it agrees wherever it parses.

Line 5, `"" "" "`, ends in an unterminated string. Ruff reports the pair at 5:4 from its recovered tokens, while Rerail's grammar leaves this line in a syntax-error region where AST clauses do not run (port-check source-partial). The line is invalid Python, so the two tools' recovery cannot be compared.

Ruff reports F523 on `'{0} {0}'.format(a, b)` inside the string annotation `y: "..."` because it runs expression rules over parsed string type definitions. In Rerail the call can only be reached through `parse: annotation`, and the engine refuses `formatArgs` there (compile error: "`formatArgs` is not supported inside parse (annotation trees)"). The DSL reference also lets an annotation rule nest only `parse: annotation`, not braceFormat, so there is no way to count fields against arguments inside a string annotation.
